ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a triangle WAH, with W at the lower left, H above, and A on the right. Point P is located on side HA, and line segment WP connects from vertex W to point P on side HA. There are also other line segments and point labels in the figure, but to find y, only the two segments AP and PH into which P divides HA need to be used. Reasoning: The problem gives that WP is the median of triangle WAH, so WP connects vertex W to the midpoint P of the opposite side HA. Therefore AP = PH. Also AP = 3y + 11, PH = 7y - 5, so 3y + 11 = 7y - 5. Solving gives 16 = 4y, therefore y = 4. The angle bisector and angle information do not need to be used to find y.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as triangle WAH with point P located on side HA and segment WP drawn from vertex W to P. From the text, WP is a median, so in triangle WAH it hits the opposite side HA at its midpoint. Therefore the two side pieces are equal: AP = PH. Use the given expressions AP = 3y + 11 and PH = 7y - 5, set 3y + 11 = 7y - 5, and solve to get y = 4. The angle information is not needed for y.
